sources.title: Decision amending the Decision on Visas, Gazette 37/26
sources.publisher: Official Gazette of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: The Official Gazette publishes adopted Council of Ministers Decision 87/26 of 15 April 2026. Article 1 replaces Article 19a with the named ordinary-passport cohort, 2026 dates and aggregate 60-day cap; Article 2 distinguishes the decision's entry into force from the travel window.

sources.title: Bahrain: current inbound visa rule and 2026 exception
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: This current country result is linked by the Ministry's public visa selector. The inbound paragraph and NOTE, below the separate outbound BiH-citizen table, expressly identify ordinary Bahraini passports, the 2026 seasonal window, embassy issuance and the visa requirement after 30 September 2026.
sources.supportingExcerpt: For stays in Bosnia and Herzegovina after September 30, 2026, a visa is required.

sources.title: Oman: current inbound visa rule and 2026 exception
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: This current Ministry visa-selector result separately states the inbound Omani rule, embassy issuance, ordinary-passport seasonal waiver and an express visa requirement for stays after 30 September 2026. The outbound table concerns BiH citizens and is not the evidence for this pair.
sources.supportingExcerpt: For stays in Bosnia and Herzegovina after September 30, 2026, a visa is required.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia: current inbound rule and 2026 exception
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry's current country result expressly requires an inbound visa outside the ordinary-passport seasonal waiver and after 30 September 2026. Its final diplomatic/official-passport exception is separate and is not generalized to ordinary passports.
sources.supportingExcerpt: For stays in Bosnia and Herzegovina after September 30, 2026, a visa is required.

policies.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina: Gulf seasonal waiver ends 30 September 2026
policies.summary: Bahraini, Omani and Saudi ordinary-passport holders are exempt from a visa for entry, exit, transit and stay from 1 June through 30 September 2026, with no more than 60 days of stay in total within that window.
conditions: This policy concerns ordinary passports of the three named countries; diplomatic and official document arrangements are separate.
The 60-day allowance is aggregate within the fixed seasonal window, not 60 days per entry or permission to remain beyond 30 September 2026.
The current MFA pages expressly require a visa for stays after 30 September 2026. This seasonal exemption supplies no work or residence permission.

allowedStays.label: Up to 60 days in total from 1 June through 30 September 2026
notes: All stay under this exemption must fall within the specified 2026 window; unused days do not extend the 30 September endpoint.

policies.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina: Gulf ordinary passports require a visa from 1 October 2026
policies.summary: The MFA's current Bahrain, Oman and Saudi Arabia pages expressly require a visa for stays after 30 September 2026. The passport-only ordinary visitor baseline therefore becomes visa-required on 1 October 2026.
conditions: This future-dated baseline does not displace the seasonal exemption through 30 September 2026.
The country pages distinguish ordinary passports from special documents; the Saudi diplomatic/official-passport exception is not an ordinary-passport exemption.
This is the nationality-and-ordinary-passport baseline, not a determination of separate supporting-visa, residence-document, special-passport or individual exceptional routes.
No post-season visitor stay length or electronic-issuance route is established by these sources. Obtaining a visa does not itself guarantee admission.
